validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real, correctly classified interstate FERC-jurisdictional gas transmission trunk, not a phantom or misclassified line. Confirmed by (1) FERC/DOE Final EIS (Docket Nos. CP89-634-000 et al., energy.gov, the original 1990-91 certificate proceeding — an independent federal-government origin, distinct from the applicant), (2) Iroquois's own current site (iroquois.com/natural-gas-company.asp), (3) TC Energy's TC PipeLines LP asset page (archived — this is literally the exact page the wiki's own cite_note-tc-1 points to, confirmed live via Wayback), (4) Northeast Gas Association member-pipeline description (northeastgas.org, industry-association origin, independent of the operator), (5) Rextag Corporation's independent pipeline-data page, and (6) a April 2025 Pipeline & Gas Journal article confirming the line is still operating and undergoing a live FERC-adjacent state permitting process (NYSDEC air permits for the Enhancement by Compression project). No source is GEM-derived. Status='operating' and Fuel='Gas' both confirmed by all of the above — no classification issue (it is a large-diameter interstate transmission trunk, not a gathering/feeder line). No duplicate: checked against the full 46-row roster: no other PID describes this Waddington-NY-to-Bronx/Long-Island system under another name.

validity.recommendation: Update Capacity from 500.00 MMcf/d to approximately 1,500 MMcf/d (1.5 Bcf/d) — the sheet's current figure is roughly 3x too low for the present-day system.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records Capacity=500.00 MMcf/d. This does not match ANY figure I could find for this system at ANY point in its history, and it is off by roughly 3x from the current, well-corroborated capacity. Independent sources: (1) TC Energy's own asset page (archived Sept 2023, the page the wiki cites): 'Capacity 1.5 Bcf/d' = 1,500 MMcf/d. (2) Northeast Gas Association (member-association fact sheet, independent of the operator): 'physical receipt capability of 1.7 Bcf/d.' (3) Rextag Corporation (independent commercial pipeline-data aggregator): 'System Capacity: 1.6 Bcf/d.' All three agree the system currently moves roughly 1.5-1.7 Bcf/d — none is anywhere near 500 MMcf/d. For completeness I also checked the ORIGINAL 1990-91 FERC certificate (Docket CP89-634-001): Iroquois was authorized to transport up to 575,900 Mcf/d (~576 MMcf/d) in Phase I, with initial actual deliveries around 423,000 Mcf/d — even that original design figure is higher than the sheet's 500, and the pipeline has since been expanded multiple times (compressor additions 1993-2010, plus the ExC project targeting Nov. 2023 in-service, permits still being finalized as of April 2025 per Pipeline & Gas Journal). There is no point in this pipeline's 30+ year history that the 500 MMcf/d figure matches cleanly; it reads as either a stale mid-life figure or a transcription error. I'm proposing 1,500 MMcf/d (TC Energy's own stated figure, cross-checked against two independent sources landing in the same 1.5-1.7 Bcf/d band) as the corrected value; note the small ~1.5-1.7 spread across sources reflects different measurement conventions (design vs. physical receipt capability) and should be resolved by whoever applies this against the live FERC tariff if greater precision is wanted.

validity.recommendation: Owner1 should not be a single 'Iroquois Pipeline Co' at 100% — replace with the two actual equity owners, roughly 50/50: TC Energy and Berkshire Hathaway Energy (successor to Dominion Energy's stake). Verify the exact current BHE subsidiary name and precise split before applying.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's operators/owners tab records Owner1='Iroquois Pipeline Co' at 100%. I could not find any company by that exact name; the actual pipeline-owning entity is 'Iroquois Gas Transmission System, L.P.', and ITS equity is split between two unaffiliated parent groups, not one 100% owner. TC Energy's own asset page (archived, the page the wiki cites) states: '49.3% [TC PipeLines, LP] + 0.7% held by a subsidiary of TC Energy' (= 50% TC Energy total) and '50% owned by affiliates of Dominion Energy, Inc.' A general web search independently corroborated that Dominion's stake has since transferred to Berkshire Hathaway Energy (Dominion sold its gas transmission and storage business to BHE in 2020), consistent with more recent language describing the co-owner as 'affiliates of Berkshire Hathaway Energy.' Rextag Corporation (independent data aggregator) separately lists TC PipeLines (49.34%) and Berkshire (24.07%) plus a residual TransCanada 0.66% stake — Rextag's percentages don't sum to 100% (likely a stale/partial scrape) so I'm not using its exact split, but it independently corroborates the qualitative fact that TWO unrelated groups (TC-affiliated and Berkshire-affiliated) hold the equity, not one 'Iroquois Pipeline Co.' Whoever applies this should pin down BHE's exact current holding-subsidiary name (e.g., via a current SEC/FERC ownership disclosure) before pasting — I did not verify that name to primary-source certainty.

validity.recommendation: Fix StartCountryOrArea from 'Canada' to 'United States' — Waddington is a New York State town on the US side of the St. Lawrence River border; StartState/Province already correctly says 'New York', which contradicts a 'Canada' country value.
validity.researcher_notes: The worklist's Location cluster carries StartState/Province='New York' but StartCountryOrArea='Canada' — an internal contradiction (New York is a US state, never a Canadian province). Every source I read is unambiguous that Waddington, NY is the US-side interconnect point where the Iroquois pipeline receives gas from TransCanada's Canadian mainline across the St. Lawrence River: iroquois.com ('the U.S.-Canadian border at Waddington, NY'), the Iroquois facilities-list PDF ('Waddington Meter Station, Waddington, NY... Interstate Pipeline Interconnect: TransCanada PipeLines'), and the original FERC/DOE EIS ('begin at the United States-Canadian border near Waddington, New York'). Waddington is the US receipt point, not a location in Canada. This should simply read 'United States', matching EndCountryOrArea (already correct) and StartState/Province (already correct).

validity.recommendation: No action — length is correct within normal rounding.
validity.researcher_notes: LengthKnown=669 km (415.8 mi) is confirmed. Multiple independent current sources describe the system as '414 miles' (iroquois.com, TC Energy's own page in one spot, Rextag) or '416 miles' (Northeast Gas Association, and TC Energy's own page elsewhere on the same archived snapshot — TC Energy is internally inconsistent between 414mi/667km and 416mi/669km in its own copy). GEM's 669 km matches TC Energy's own 416-mile/669-km figure exactly. This is the CURRENT total-system length (mainline + the Long Island Sound crossing + the Northport/South Commack area + the Eastchester Extension lateral to Hunts Point, Bronx, which per the Iroquois facilities-list PDF came into service Feb. 2004) — not the original 1990-92 Phase I construction length of 369.4 miles cited in the FERC/DOE EIS, which is a different, earlier-vintage figure and not in conflict with the current total.

cross_row_leads.facts: The same 1990-91 FERC/DOE Final EIS that covers Iroquois's original Phase I certificate also covers a contemporaneous Algonquin Gas Transmission capacity-expansion application (Docket No. CP89-661-000, amended CP89-661-001) to transport up to 432,204 Mcfd (later 245,950 Mcfd) of Canadian/domestic gas for Iroquois/Tennessee and ANR project customers — this is a 1989-90 vintage Algonquin expansion filing, NOT the modern 'AIM' (Algonquin Incremental Market, ~2015-17) project that P0150 tracks, and may or may not correspond cleanly to P0149's 'Main Line' segment; flagging for whoever works Algonquin next rather than asserting a match myself.

summary: P0205 (Iroquois Gas Pipeline) is real, correctly classified, and unique on the roster (confirmed, tier high, no duplicate) — but Capacity (500 MMcf/d, should be ~1,500 MMcf/d, a 3x understatement), Owner1 (100% 'Iroquois Pipeline Co', should be ~50/50 TC Energy / Berkshire Hathaway Energy), and StartCountryOrArea ('Canada', should be 'United States' — contradicts its own StartState/Province='New York') are all flagged as concerns with contested candidates; filled Diameter (24, 30 in), Pressure (1440 psig), ConstructionYear (1991), ProposalYear (1989) and Operator (Iroquois Pipeline Operating Company) from the original FERC/DOE EIS and iroquois.com; SegmentCost is UNRESOLVED (no cost figure found).
